frontier.hypothesis: The v0<->v1 wall is a local-before-global pass-ordering invariant: at 43 insns no cheat-free C can put the multi-death reused load-web in $v0 while the single-death mask takes $v1, because local-alloc (mask) always precedes global-alloc (web).
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c:472 routes the reused web (deaths=3) to global and the interleaved mask (deaths=1, one block) to local; find_free_reg gives the local mask the lowest free reg ($v0); the global web then conflicts with $v0 and takes $v1. Equalizing the pass (mask->global needs +1 death/store or +1 block/branch; web->local needs no-reuse which breaks the interleave) is impossible at 43 insns.
